top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a single coherent achievement: the magic-wavelength lattice lets many neutral atoms be interrogated with the light shift cancelled, which the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes did not credit. Ye's record 1e-18 accuracy and many-body clock physics have been confirmed independently in Sr, Yb and Hg. The two-name allocation (Katori for the concept, Ye for the performance) is the cleanest available, and the citation can name demonstrated performance and physics yield rather than the pending redefinition of the second. The clock alone is preferable to a pairing with a one-name IceCube part, whose credit would look arbitrary; P002 still keeps the clock and ranks second, ahead of the condensed-matter options. P004 (topological insulators) is mature but has the 2016 overlap and the Hasan/Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang credit gap. P003 (twisted bilayer graphene) is premature while the mechanism is unsettled. No award is last since a clean, mature option exists.
recusal_note: No documented tie to Katori, Ye or any laureate in the slate. Profile-based conflict is only with circuit QED (B023: WACQT director, Chalmers superconducting-circuit colleagues), which is not in the slate.
